questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find a job working from home
Predictions about the future of work and how reliable they are
Why robots have already replaced most workers
The life, companies and ideas of the tech billionaire Elon Musk
questions.why: They ask what work will be like in the future and hear experts doubt many predictions.

questions.q: Why does Beth mention smell-o-vision and a miracle pill?
options: To describe new inventions coming soon
To show how technology changed work
To explain what daily life was like in the 1930s
To show predictions often don't come true
questions.why: She says these were predicted in the 1930s but so far haven't come true.

questions.q: What did Elon Musk recently predict?
options: Everyone will work a four-day week
Robots will be banned from offices
AI will eventually mean nobody has to work
People will stop working from home after Covid
questions.why: Neil says Musk predicted AI will eventually mean that no one will have to work.

questions.q: Which prediction about work came true during Covid?
options: Millions of people worked from home
Robots took over most jobs
Working hours fell by half
Everyone moved to a four-day working week
questions.why: Beth says during Covid millions were forced to work from home.

questions.q: What is Professor Brendan Burchell's attitude to predictions about work?
options: He doubts them, as past predictions were often wrong
He believes most of them
He thinks only economists are able to make good predictions
He thinks Elon Musk is right
questions.why: He says “we have to be sceptical” because the track record isn't good.

questions.q: What does Burchell say about predictions of much shorter working hours?
options: They came true in the 1930s
Working hours have actually gone up a lot over recent years
They have finally come true since Covid
We're slowly moving that way, but big changes haven't come
questions.why: He says we're heading very gradually in that direction, but the large changes haven't come to pass.

questions.q: What does Andrew Palmer think about AI and jobs?
options: AI will get rid of all jobs
AI will affect some jobs, but won't remove them all
AI will have no effect on jobs
AI will only create new jobs and never remove any old ones
questions.why: He says he doesn't think AI will get rid of all jobs, though some professions are at risk.

options: Workers won't want to do the new jobs that AI creates
Economists will stop studying jobs
New jobs may not appear as quickly as old ones go
Companies won't be able to afford AI
questions.why: He worries about a sequencing risk – new jobs won't necessarily come at the same time.
